Order 
T his i s second application under section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure, for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant relating to FIR/Crime No.185/2021 dated 17.11.2021 registered at Police Station- Budera, District- Tikamgarh, for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 376(2)(n), 342,
323, 506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5/6 and 17 of POCSO Act.
His previous application was dismissed for want of prosecution vide order dated 31.10.2022.
Another application for bail in connected case i.e. M.Cr.C. No.53305/2022 has been withdrawn by father of the applicant.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 28.03.2022.
He submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
He further submits that challan has been filed.
The applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Trial will take considerable time to conclude.

Upon these submissions, learned counsel prays that the applicant may be released Suraj Raikwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102023362/
1 on bail.

sentences.text: On the contrary, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the bail application.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
Prosecution case is that prosecutrix was abducted and sexually abused by the applicant.
The FSL report has positive indications.
It appears from the statements of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. that she accompanied the applicant to various places and stayed in his company for atleast four months.
She never raised any alarm in that period to resist the overtures of the applicant.
Her date of birth is 12.08.2005, which suggests that she had completed 17 years of age at the time of incident.

Considering the age of prosecutrix as well as the fact of consensual relationship of prosecutrix and applicant, I find it appropriate to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
